```{r}
#| label: setup
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
source(file.path("..", "Figure_Data", "FigureABM.R"))

R0_VALUES <- c(5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17)
MEASURES  <- c(
  size  = "Final outbreak size (infections)",
  share = "Runs with 10 or more cases (%)"
)

fmt <- function(x) formatC(round(x), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
```

```{r}
#| label: data
sizes <- rbindlist(lapply(R0_VALUES, function(r0) {
  s <- abm_summaries(".", r0)
  s$final[,
    .(
      median = median(outbreak_size),
      q25    = quantile(outbreak_size, 0.25, names = FALSE),
      q75    = quantile(outbreak_size, 0.75, names = FALSE)
    ),
    by = scenario
  ][s$runs, on = "scenario"][, r0 := r0]
}))
```

The three focal scenarios of the main analysis (`make scenarios`) for R0 = 5, 7, ..., 17, with the POLYMOD contact matrix, no isolation willingness, and 90% quarantine willingness:

- No interventions: no rash contact reduction and no contact tracing.
- Self-isolation only: 50% rash contact reduction, no contact tracing.
- Self-isolation with quarantine: 75% rash contact reduction and 25% contact-tracing success, with a 21-day quarantine.

As in Figure 4 (R0 = 9), self-isolation with quarantine uses the run with quarantine and the other two scenarios the run without. Each scenario has 1,000 runs; runs with fewer than `r MIN_OUTBREAK_SIZE` cases are early extinctions, and the final outbreak sizes are over the remaining (retained) runs.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-scenarios
tab <- sizes[order(r0, scenario), .(
  r0, scenario,
  retained = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", fmt(retained), 100 * retained / runs),
  size     = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt(median), fmt(q25), fmt(q75))
)]

kable(
  tab,
  col.names = c("R0", "Scenario", "Retained runs (%)", "Infections"),
  align     = "rlrr",
  caption   = paste(
    "Runs with 10 or more cases out of 1,000, and final outbreak size at",
    "day 365, median (interquartile range) across those runs."
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-scenarios
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Final outbreak size at day 365 (median and interquartile range across the retained runs) and share of runs with 10 or more cases, by R0. The dashed line marks R0 = 9, the runs of Figure 4."
fig_data <- rbind(
  sizes[, .(
    r0, scenario,
    measure = MEASURES[["size"]],
    value   = median,
    q25,
    q75
  )],
  sizes[, .(
    r0, scenario,
    measure = MEASURES[["share"]],
    value   = 100 * retained / runs,
    q25     = NA_real_,
    q75     = NA_real_
  )]
)
fig_data[, measure := factor(measure, MEASURES)]

ggplot(fig_data, aes(r0, value, color = scenario)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 9,
    color      = INK_SECONDARY,
    linetype   = "dashed",
    linewidth  = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
    size      = 0.35,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    na.rm     = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = SCENARIO_COLORS) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = R0_VALUES) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "R0", y = NULL) +
  theme_figure4() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = INK_PRIMARY))
```
